key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on the chemical species present and their addition sequence: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide provides surface passivation.
engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor chemistry and mixing order could help preserve MXenes during perovskite solar-cell fabrication.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to track surface chemistry.
Apply density functional theory to investigate adsorption interactions.
evidence_signal: Combined XPS analysis and DFT calculations support rapid degradation by iodine and polyiodides, slower PbI2-induced oxidation, and hydrogen-bond-mediated stabilization by MAI.
watch_item: The abstract reports model-ink chemistry, not quantified device-performance gains or long-term solar-cell stability.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
